chunks: Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn al-Nu'man al-Ahwal, Sahib al-Taqq, from Sallam ibn al-Mustanir from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The affection of the believer for the believer for the sake of Allah is from the greatest of the branches of faith. Indeed! And whoever loves for the sake of Allah and hates for the sake of Allah and gives for the sake of Allah and withholds for the sake of Allah, then he is from the elites of Allah.'

key_terms.أَصْفِيَاءِ اللَّهِ: Elites or chosen ones of Allah
key_terms.فِي اللَّهِ: For the sake of Allah / Regarding Allah

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to love and hate for the sake of Allah in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi elucidates the Shia concept of 'Al-Wadud fi Allah' (love for the sake of God), distinguishing it from mere social affection by anchoring it in divine criteria. It highlights that true believers align their emotional attachments and material generosity with Allah's pleasure, a trait that marks them as 'Asfiya' (the chosen elite). This principle underscores the integration of spiritual devotion with social conduct in Shia ethical tradition.
